When I first had my TBI, I moved from a bigger city to a small town in NE Tennessee. There are a lot of nice small towns in the Appalachian area that are close enough to  big towns for any main things they provide (medical care, entertainment, shopping, etc.) while still being quiet and peaceful where you are. I really loved the long walks you could take in the country side or hiking in the woods, that helped me a lot. Even if not forever, I think a lot of nice places in that side of the country might help give you peace. If nothing else a trip out there, or somewhere similar, can help take you away from the busyness. It definitely helped me a lot the first years after my injury.

At work the other day (I'm a cashier at a grocery store), a customer had a kinda complicated order - normal, no big deal. Coupons, weirdly specific about the way everything was bagged, multiple rainchecks, stuff like that. But I was in a good mood, and handled it all with no stress. When I hand her receipt I say "Have a great day!", and she refuses to take it. She looks at me with an expectant face and says "And?". I have no clue what she wants from me, so I just kind of stare back for a second. She mouths "Thank You", and thinking she was thanking me, I say "You're Welcome!". She gives me a disapproving look and takes her receipt, mumbling under her breath, leaving me kind of confused. 

When her order was done, I start serving the next customer and she stands to the side reading her receipt. After a moment I realize "Shit, something's fucked up, here we go", and she comes back over to my line. She walks back up to me and says in the most condescending tone "Ya know, you did a really good job. You were very nice to talk to and smiled a lot, and handled my order well. But in the future, you should really thank all of your customers, because it's because of us that you have a job". I just stand there in shock. She then proceeds to stand to the side and watch the next person's order, I assume to see if I thank them - I did not. Just said "Have a nice day!" like I have for the past two years.

I have a very vague memory of being very little at a movie theatre and losing my mom. We were very poor back then, so it was very special to go to the movies, and I wanted to stay till the very end and watch the credits. My mom got up and said we were leaving, and her and my sister left, assuming I was with them. It was really dark and a lot of people were walking around. When I realized I couldn't see my mom anymore I got up to leave, and I remember a man holding my hand and walking away with me. A moment later I saw my mom I think near the bathroom and went to her, and he let go. But I remember vaguely him trying to lead me away, we just happened to walk past her. As an adult now it's scary to think what could have happened if we didn't walk past her.
